title: Ladder Pulls
description:
Ladder pulls are one of CRL's largest architectural hardware categories, but sales fell 13% from 2022 to 2023 as competitors sold similar-looking pulls for close to half the price. Customers didn't understand why ours cost more.

Instead of racing to the bottom, we split the line in two. CRL X is a premium exterior pull in 3 mm, marine-grade 316 stainless for coastal and winter climates, priced against the market's premium brand. CRL I is a 1.5 mm, 304 stainless interior pull at a value price. Both come from a new supplier with a lower cost structure. We focused on the fast-moving sizes, planned a sell-down of the old stock, ran first-article inspections on every component, and took the program through Gate 3 to stocked inventory in spring 2026.

brief.label: Problem
brief.text: Competitors offered lower-quality pulls at prices close to ours or far below, and customers weren't told why CRL's cost more.

brief.label: Strategy
brief.text: Two lines for two applications: premium exterior and value interior, which limits cannibalization between them.

brief.label: Solution
brief.text: CRL X (316 stainless, 3 mm) for exterior and harsh environments; CRL I (304 stainless, 1.5 mm) for interiors. Both replace the previous line.

brief.label: Customers
brief.text: Architects, temperers, glazing contractors and Division 10 contractors.

brief.label: Market
brief.text: Glass office market over $20B, growing 3.8% a year.

quotes.quote: As an owner I am looking for ways to help maximize profit. I must buy ladder pulls from [a low-cost competitor] since they are a significant price difference. I'm not able to justify spending more when I can spend much less for similar results.

recovery_title: Plan to win back ladder pull sales
recovery_intro: Sales had fallen every year since 2022, and slow-moving sizes sat on the shelf for anywhere from 4 to 62 months. Matching low-cost pulls on price would have meant matching them on quality too.

recovery.label: Split the line
recovery.text: CRL X, 3 mm 316 marine-grade stainless for exteriors and harsh climates, priced against the market's premium brand; CRL I, 1.5 mm 304 stainless for interiors at a value price.

recovery.label: Explain the price
recovery.text: Sales materials lead with material and wall thickness, so customers can see why a coastal or winter-climate entrance needs the exterior pull.

recovery.label: Clear the old stock
recovery.text: Discount the previous line hard while it still sells, then move the remainder in one bulk sale to recover what was spent.

recovery.label: Buy smarter
recovery.text: A new supplier with a lower cost structure, and stocking focused on the lengths that drive most of the revenue.

challenges.challenge: The new supplier's long lead time meant waiting for the usual post-launch buy would leave a gap on the shelf.
challenges.resolution: I prepared an early initial purchase order with the new parts and product categories, the same approach we had used on TurboFlex, and got leadership approval ahead of the normal cycle.

challenges.challenge: First articles passed dimensional and fit checks, but the assemblies didn't match the drawings on parts and quantities, and parts shifted inside the box.
challenges.resolution: Quality and I documented every gap on the inspection reports, sent drawing corrections and missing-part lists back to the supplier, and added packing material and proper box labels before the production run.
